Rashi on Zevachim 19a:10:1.hebrew: לימא פליג - רבא דרבא אדר' יהודה? דאילו רבי יוחנן פשיטא לן דפליג עליה, ואפילו צילצול קטן מכשר, דהא עלה קמהדר ופליג. אלא דרבא דאיתמר (עלה) בעלמא, מי לימא פליג אדרבי יהודה, דנימא דרבא אפי' צילצול קטן מכשר שלא במקום בגדים:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:10:1.english: Let us say that he disagrees - [that is,] Rava, with Rabbi Yehuda? For Rabbi Yoḥanan, it is obvious to us that he disagrees with him, and [holds that] even a small sash is valid [as not interposing], for he was going around on this [issue] and disagreeing. Rather, regarding Rava's [statement] that was said elsewhere, [the Gemara asks]: Shall we say that he disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda, so that we would say that according to Rava even a small sash is valid when [worn] not in the place of the garments?

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:11:1.hebrew: ולר' יוחנן - דקאמר אפי' צילצול לא חייץ, מאי איריא דנקט תנא דמתני' גמי? לשמועינן צילצול לא הוי ייתור, וכל שכן גמי:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:11:1.english: And according to Rabbi Yochanan - who said that even a sash does not constitute an interposition, why does the Tanna of our Mishnah specifically mention a reed? Let him teach us [that] a sash is not [considered] an extra [addition], and all the more so a reed.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:11:2.hebrew: דגמי מסי - רופא את המכה, ואפ"ה מותר, דאין שבות במקדש. דכולה מסכתא באיסור שבת איירי, ועיקר משום שבות נקט לה. ומשנה זו בעירובין, וכן כולה הך סוגיא התם היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:11:2.english: That a reed heals - It heals the wound, and nevertheless it is permitted, since there is no [rabbinic] Shabbat prohibition (shevut) in the Temple. For the entire tractate deals with the prohibition of Shabbat, and it mentioned it mainly because of [the issue of] shevut. And this mishna [is discussed] in [tractate] Eruvin, and likewise this entire passage is [discussed] there.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:12:1.hebrew: נכנסה לו רוח בבגדו - והבדילתו מבשרו בשעת עבודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:12:1.english: A gust of wind entered his garment - And it separated it from his flesh during the service.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:14:1.english: It is a growth - Behold, it is like his flesh.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:14:2.hebrew: כיון דקפיד עלה - דברצונו לא תהא בבשרו:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:14:2.english: Since he objects to it - For it is his wish that it not be on his flesh.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:15:1.hebrew: אבק עפר - דק, ואינו מרגיש בו:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:15:1.english: Dust of dirt - [It is] fine, and one does not feel it.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:16:1.hebrew: בית השחי מהו שיחוץ - אויר בית השחי, כגון בתי זרועותיו של חלוקו שהוא רחב ואינו נוגע בבית השחי, מהו שיחוץ? וצריך שיהו בתי זרועותיו דחוקים ונוגעין בבשר:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:16:1.english: The armpit — what is [the law] that it interposes - The air space of the armpit, such as the sleeves of his tunic, which is wide and does not touch the armpit: what is [the law] that it interposes? [The question arises because] it is necessary that its sleeves be tight and touching the flesh.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:17:1.english: His body - His hand, which is his body.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:18:1.english: Let us say - This implies that it comes from elsewhere [i.e., it is a foreign thread that was not part of the vestment].

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:18:2.hebrew: נימא מדולדלת - מן הבגד, מגוררין ותחובה בו קצת, אלא שנתקה מעיקרא:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:18:2.english: A hanging thread - from the garment; [it is] frayed and is slightly lodged in it, except that it was [already] severed at its base.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:19:1.hebrew: יצא שערו - מראשו למטה, עד שנכנס בין כתונת לבשרו, מהו? את"ל ידו לא חייצא, שערו מאי?:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:19:1.english: His hair emerged - from his head downward, until it entered between the tunic and his flesh, what is [the law]? If you say [that] his hand does not interpose, [what about] his hair that emerged — what [is the law]?

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:1:1.hebrew: כנגד אצילי ידיהם - על צלעותיהן, כנגד המרפק:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:1:1.english: Opposite the elbows of their hands - On their sides, opposite the elbow.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:1.hebrew: מהו שיחוצו - השאלה היא למיהוי ייתור בגדים:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:1.english: What is [the halakha] that they interpose - [The question is] whether they are to be considered an extra garment.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:2.hebrew: אליבא דמ"ד - בפרק בתרא דעירובין (דף צו.) ובהקומץ רבה (מנחות לו:):
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:2.english: According to the one who says - [This is discussed] in the last chapter of Eruvin (page 96a) and in [the chapter] Hakometz Rabbah (Menachot 36b).

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:3.hebrew: דיום נמי חייצי - דאל"כ, מצינו עבודות לילה חמיר מעבודות יום, והן קלים מהן:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:3.english: That by day they also interpose - For if not, we would find that nighttime service is more stringent than daytime service, whereas they are [in fact] lighter than them.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:4.hebrew: לא תבעי לך - דודאי חייצי, כדמפרש טעמא: כיון דבעבודות לילה חייצין, דהא לא מצוה הוה דניהוי כגופיה משום חביבותא דמצות:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:20:4.english: Do not raise the dilemma - For certainly they interpose, as [the Gemara] explains the reason: Since they interpose in the service at night, for it is not a mitzva that would be considered as [part of] his body because of the mitzva's dearness.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:22:1.english: And Levites on their platform - To sing [the Temple songs].

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:22:3.hebrew: פטורין מן התפלה - (שאין יכולין לכוין):
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:22:3.english: Exempt from prayer - (For they are unable to concentrate [their thoughts].)

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:22:4.hebrew: ומן התפילין - דקיימא לן (סוכה דף כה.) העוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:22:4.english: And from phylacteries - For we hold (Sukkah 25a) that one who is engaged in [performing] a mitzvah is exempt from [another] mitzvah.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:23:1.hebrew: דלא מיתני ליה אסורין - שאין יכול לשנות בהן איסור:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:23:1.english: That it cannot teach "prohibited" [regarding] them - For one cannot teach a prohibition with respect to them.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:24:1.hebrew: דיד - חוצצות, דהוא בין בגד לבשר:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:24:1.english: Of the hand - They interpose, for it [the phylactery of the hand] is between the garment and the flesh.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:25:1.hebrew: אמר ממלכת כהנים כתיב בכו - וצריכין אתם לנהוג עצמכם בתפארת של כהנים, דכתיב בהו לא יחגרו ביזע:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:25:1.english: He said: “A kingdom of priests” is written regarding you - And you must conduct yourselves with the splendor of the priests, regarding whom it is written: “They shall not gird themselves with [anything that causes] sweat.”

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:25:2.hebrew: דראש - תפילין של ראש אין חוצצות, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:25:2.english: For the head - [The phylacteries of the head] do not interpose, as [the Gemara] explains as it proceeds.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:26:1.hebrew: שערו - שער של כהן גדול שהיה נראה בין ציץ שעל מצחו למצנפת שבגובה ראשו:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:26:1.english: His hair - [the hair] of the High Priest that was visible between the frontplate that was on his forehead and the mitre that was at the top of his head.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:2:1.hebrew: איזגדר מלכא - כך שמו, ומלך פרס היה:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:2:1.english: Izgadar the king - That was his name, and he was a king of Persia.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:2:2.hebrew: והוה מידלי המיינאי ותיתייה ניהליה - אבנטו היה גבוה, חגור מלמעלה מכנגד אצילי ידיו, והפשיטו למטה כדי לנאותו:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:2:2.english: And my belt was raised, and he lowered it - His belt was high, girded above, opposite the joints of his arms [i.e., his elbows]; and he pulled it down lower in order to make him look dignified.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:3:1.hebrew: כורך עליה גמי - בשעת עבודה, שגנאי הוא שתראה שם מכתו. ואע"ג דגמי מסי מכה, וכל דבר שיש בו משום רפואה אסור משום שבות — גזירה שמא ישחוק סמנים — ה"מ במדינה, אבל במקדש לא גזרו משום שבות:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:3:1.english: He wraps a reed around it - During the time of the service, for it is a disgrace that his wound be seen there. And although a reed heals a wound, and anything that involves medical treatment is prohibited as a rabbinic prohibition (shevut) — a decree lest one grind herbs — this applies only in the country, but in the Temple they did not decree [a prohibition] on account of shevut.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:3:2.english: But if to draw blood - That he intends for this.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:3:3.hebrew: כאן וכאן אסור - דחבורה הוא, ואיסור דאורייתא:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:3:3.english: Here and there it is prohibited - For it is a wound, and [the prohibition] is by Torah law.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:4:2.hebrew: אבל שלא במקום בגדים - כגון אצבע:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:4:2.english: But not in a place of [the priestly] garments - For example, a finger.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:5:1.hebrew: ותיפוק לי משום דחוצץ - בין ידו לעבודה, ואסור, דבעינן ולקח הכהן — שתהא קבלה בעצמו של כהן. והיכי שרי ר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:5:1.english: And let [him] derive it [from the fact] that it is an interposition - between his hand and the service, and it is forbidden, since we require [the verse] "and the priest shall take" — that the receiving be with the priest's own body. So how did Rabbi Yochanan permit it?

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:5:2.english: On the left [hand] - which is not fit for the service.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:5:3.hebrew: שלא במקום עבודה - כגון על גב היד:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:5:3.english: Not in a place of service - For example, on the back of the hand.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:6:1.english: And it disagrees with [the statement of] Rava - with [the statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:6:2.hebrew: שלש על שלש חוצצות - כלומר, הוי ייתור בגדים. ואיידי דנקט בנימא אחת במקום בגדים לישנא דחציצה דשייכא בה, נקט נמי במסקנא לישנא דחציצה:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:6:2.english: Three by three interpose - That is, it is an excess of garments [i.e., it constitutes an additional garment]. And because [Rava] used, regarding a single thread in the place of the garments, the term of interposition, which is applicable there, he also used the term of interposition in the conclusion [regarding three by three].

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:7:1.hebrew: ודאי פליגא - דהא אמר [שלא במקום בגדים] לא הוי ייתור בגדים, ואפי' שלש על שלש במשמע:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:7:1.english: Certainly he disagrees - For he said that [fabric in a place other than where the vestments are worn] is not an interposition of the vestments, and even [fabric of] three by three [fingerbreadths] is included.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:7:2.hebrew: מי לימא דפליגא - דאיהו אמר צילצול קטן חוצץ, ורבא אמר: פחות משלש לא חוצץ:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:7:2.english: Shall we say that he disagrees - For he [Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Chiyya] said that a small sash is an interposition, whereas Rava said that [a sash of] less than three [fingerbreadths] is not an interposition.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:8:1.hebrew: דחשיב - לפי שעשוי לנוי, והוי בגד:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:8:1.english: Since it is significant - Because it is made for adornment, and it is [considered] a garment.

Rashi on Zevachim 19a:9:1.hebrew: ל"א אמרי לה כו' - בדר' יהודה בר' חייא לא פליגי לישני. דחוצץ נמי דקאמר, משום ייתור בגדים הוא, דלא שייכא למימר חציצה שלא במקום בגדים ושלא במקום עבודה, דאי במקום עבודה אפי' נימא חייצא. ובדר' יוחנן הוא דפליגי לישני:
Rashi on Zevachim 19a:9:1.english: Another version: “Some say” etc. - Regarding [the statement of] Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, the two versions do not disagree. For [in the second version,] what he said, “it interposes,” is also on account of the excess [width] of the vestments; for it is not applicable to speak of interposition in a place outside the vestments and outside the place of the service, since [if it were] in the place of the service, even [the first version] would say that it interposes. And it is regarding [the statement of] Rabbi Yoḥanan that the two versions disagree.

Tosafot on Zevachim 19a:11:1.hebrew: מאי איריא גמי לשמועינן צילצול קטן - תימה: הא איצטריך לאשמועינן גמי משום דין אבל לא במדינה, דטעמא דשחיקת סמנים לא שייך בצילצול, דהא לא מסי. וי"ל דמ"מ הוה ליה לאשמועינן צילצול, דהוי חידוש גדול יותר, דלא הוי ייתור בגדים, מלאשמועינן איסור של גמי במדינה. ומשני דקמ"ל דגמי מסי, משום לשון חכמים מרפא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 19a:11:1.english: Why specifically a reed? Let it teach us [about] a small sash - This is puzzling: Surely it was necessary to teach us about a reed because of [the law of] a mourner, but not in the provinces [outside the Temple], since the reason of grinding spices does not apply to a sash, as it does not heal. And one can answer that nevertheless it should have taught us [about] a sash, which is a greater novelty — that it is not an excess of garments — rather than teach us the prohibition of a reed in the provinces. And [the Gemara] answers that it teaches us that a reed heals, based on [the verse] "the tongue of the wise is healing."

Tosafot on Zevachim 19a:20:1.hebrew: תפלין מהו שיחוצו - פירש בקונטרס: שהספק הוא למיהוי ייתור בגדים. ואי אפשר לומר כן, דהא קאמר לימוד ערוך דתפילין חוצצות, ובשל יד איירי; דבשל ראש הא אמרינן בסמוך דאין חוצצות. ואי משום ייתור בגדים — אפי' דראש נמי! ומיהו למאן דאמר לעיל "לא אמרו ייתור בגדים אלא במקום בגדים, אבל שלא במקום בגדים לא" ניחא, דשל יד הוי במקום בגדים ולא של ראש. ומשום חציצה ממש נראה טפי, כדדריש בסמוך "על בשרו" — שלא יהא דבר חוצץ. מיהו הא דתניא "אינן חוצצות", ואוקמינן לה בשל ראש — לא הוי שום חידוש שלא יהא חציצה, כי אם שאינן [משום] ייתור בגדים; אם לא דתאמר דקמ"ל דשערו היה נראה, א"נ קמ"ל דלא חציצי תחת פתילי הציץ:
Tosafot on Zevachim 19a:20:1.english: Phylacteries — what is the law as to whether they interpose - Rashi explained in the Kuntres [that the question is] whether this counts as an excess of garments. But it is impossible to say so, for [the Gemara] says, "a well-established teaching," that phylacteries interpose, and it is speaking of the arm phylactery; for regarding the head phylactery, we say shortly afterward that they do not interpose. And if it were because of an excess of garments — [it would apply] even to the head phylactery as well! However, according to the one who said earlier, "They only spoke of an excess of garments in a place of garments, but not in a place that is not [a place] of garments," it works out well, since the arm phylactery is in a place of garments, and the head phylactery is not. And it appears more likely [that the question is] about actual interposition, as [the Gemara] expounds shortly afterward "upon his flesh" — that nothing should interpose. Nevertheless, regarding that which was taught, "They do not interpose," which we established as referring to the head phylactery — it would not be any novelty that there is no interposition, except that they are not [forbidden] because of an excess of garments; unless you say that it comes to teach us that his hair was visible, or alternatively that it comes to teach us that they do not interpose beneath the threads of the head-plate:

Tosafot on Zevachim 19a:3:1.hebrew: כורך עליה גמי במקדש אבל לא במדינה - פי' בקונט': גמי מרפא, ואסור משום שחיקת סמנים. ונראה לפרש: גזירה אטו להוציא דם. וכן בכל הנהו (דעירובין (דף קג.) יש לפרש טעמא) דאסירי במדינה — משום איסורא דקתני בתר הכי: כאן וכאן אסור. ומיהו בירושלמי משמע דטעמא משום שחיקת סמנין, דמסיק פרק כל כתבי הקודש גבי רבי שלקה באצבעו בשבת, ונתן עליה ספוג יבש וקשר עליה גמי מבחוץ, וקאמר התם דלמדנו דספוג אינו מרפא אלא משמר, גמי לפי שהוא מן המוכן. ובסמוך נמי קאמר "קא משמע לן דגמי מסי", משמע דהיינו טעמא דאבל לא במדינה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 19a:3:1.english: "He wraps a reed around it in the Temple, but not in the country" - Rashi explained in his commentary: A reed heals, and it is prohibited because of the grinding of medicinal herbs. But it appears to explain [it as] a decree lest he come to draw blood. And so too in all of these [cases] (in Eiruvin (103a) the reason should be explained [this way]) that are prohibited in the country — [it is] because of the prohibition that [the Mishnah] teaches afterward: "Here and there it is prohibited." However, in the Jerusalem Talmud it implies that the reason is because of grinding medicinal herbs, as it concludes in the chapter "Kol Kitvei HaKodesh," regarding Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who was injured on his finger on Shabbat, and placed a dry sponge on it and tied a reed around it on the outside. And [the Jerusalem Talmud] says there that we learn that a sponge does not heal but [only] protects, [and that they used] a reed because it is [considered] prepared [for use on Shabbat]. And shortly afterward it also says, "This teaches us that a reed heals," which implies that this is the reason for "but not in the country."
